searchText: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/pull/172#issuecomment-1033131094 I later added a variable-time inversion https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/blob/1c5341fd7e8af9084223b5bce616b4a8262eab14/constantine/math/arithmetic/limbs_exgcd.nim#L684 It's significantly faster than GMP. Writeup: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/blob/85b00a1/doc/safegcd_implementation.md Good docs, thanks. I wonder if this is implementable in EVM. The main speedup of both Bernstein-Yang (libsecp256k1 and Constantine) and Pornin (BLST and Gnark) algorithms is doing the computations on 62 bits at a time instead of the full 254 bits. For EVM we want exactly the opposite: use 256-bit values preferably.
